sentences.text:
Heard Sri Ajay Tripathi, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Ashok Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the O.P. No.2.
2.

I find merit in the argument of learned counsel for the applicant that not only impugned order passed under Section 204 Cr.P.C. is bereft of reasons as required under Section 204 Cr.P.C. that there are sufficient ground to proceed against applicant as well as that even cognizance of offence taken under Sections 420 and 406 I.P.C. are barred in terms of provisions of Section 468 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: Aforesaid submissions also have support from factual aspect of case that a friendly loan was taken by complainant from applicant in the year 2002, which was allegedly repaid, however, the cheques given by complainant were not returned by applicant, which later on were encashed in year 2015.
Complainant had knowledge of said withdrawal, however, he waited thereafter for about 7 years and filed a criminal complaint under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. on 15.11.2022.
There is no allegation of continuance offence, therefore, proceedings are barred under Section 468 Cr.P.C..
at least for Section 406 I.P.C. is concerned

For reference, Section 468 Cr.P.C. is reproduced hereinafter:
" Section 468 - Bar to taking cognizance after lapse of the period of limitation:
1.
Except as otherwise provided elsewhere in this Code, no Court, shall take cognizance of an offence of the category specified in Sub-Section (2), after the expiry of the period of limitation.

Learned counsel for the O.P. No.2 has tried to convince the Court, but miserably failed that not only facts of the present case are against him, but on position of law also.
5.

  Fiona Shrikhande v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2014 SC 957, it was observed as laid down under "We are, in this case, concerned only with the question as to whether, on a reading of the complaint, a prima facie case has been made out or not to issue process by the Magistrate

entities.text: Fiona Shrikhande v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2014 SC 957
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The law as regards issuance of process in criminal cases is well settled.

At the complaint stage, the Magistrate is merely concerned with the allegations made out in the complaint and has only to prima facie satisfy whether there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the accused and it is not the province of the Magistrate to enquire into a detailed discussion on the merits or demerits of the case.

The scope of enquiry under Section 202 is extremely limited in the sense that the Magistrate, at this stage, is expected to examine prima facie the truth or falsehood of the allegations made in the complaint.
Magistrate is

not expected to embark upon a detailed discussion of the merits or demerits of the case,
but only consider the inherent probabilities apparent on the statement made in the complaint."

6.

I have carefully perused above referred impugned order which has been passed in a very cursory manner by learned Trial Court and has summoned the applicant for offence under Sections 420 and 406 I.P.C. without even considering the facts of the case as well as without even referring contents of complaint, statement of complaint and witnesses recorded under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.
7.

Above referred impugned order is in the teeth of judgment passed by Supreme Court in Lalankumar Singh and others vs. State of Maharashtra, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1383 that it is bereft of Subhash Chandra Sharma vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: requisite reasoning and there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the applicant.
For reference relevant part of Lalankumar Singh is mentioned hereinafter :
"38. The order of issuance of process is not an empty formality.
The Magistrate is required to apply his mind as to whether sufficient ground for proceeding exists in the case or not.
The formation of such an opinion is required to be stated in the order itself.
The order is liable to be set aside if no reasons are given therein while coming to the conclusion that there is a prima facie case against the accused...."

8. In aforesaid circumstances, not only impugned order order is in teeth of Lalankumar Singh (supra), but learned Magistrate has failed to appreciate that there was bar to take cognizance of offences under Section 406 I.P.C. as prescribed in above referred Section 468 Cr.P.C.
There is no allegation of continuous offence.
The Court takes note that offence under Section 420 I.P.C. is punishable with 7 years.
9. In aforesaid circumstances, impugned summoning order is not legally sustainable and it is a fit case where inherent jurisdiction can be invoked.

Accordingly impugned summoning order dated 16.3.2024 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court No.5, Ghaziabad passed in Complaint Case No.4660/2023 (Shakuntala Sharma Vs. Subhash Chandra Sharma) under Sections 420 and 406 I.P.C., P.S. Sahibabad, District-Ghaziabad as well as entire proceedings of aforesaid complaint case are hereby quashed and this application is accordingly allowed.
